sqlite.secret_material: reject passwords, tokens, credentials, and private keys; persist references and digests only

migrations.up: create strict domain tables, append-only event journal, and fenced writer metadata in one transaction
migrations.down: drop domain tables and event journal; retain writer fencing metadata; set schema_version and user_version to 0

migrations.up: create per-domain cutover rows and append-only cutover journal; widen schema_version bound to 2
migrations.down: drop cutover tables and journal together with domain tables during rollback to schema 0

migrations.up: create append-only replay-safe control operation journal; widen schema_version bound to 3
migrations.down: drop operation journal together with domain and cutover tables during rollback to schema 0

migrations.up: bind storage dispatch intent to the action claim; widen schema_version bound to 4
migrations.down: drop storage dispatch intent tables during rollback to schema 0

migrations.up: create action leases and atomic resource admission; widen schema_version bound to 5
migrations.down: drop action lease and resource lease tables during rollback to schema 0

migrations.up: create the immutable action reconciliation boundary; widen schema_version bound to 6
migrations.down: drop the reconciliation boundary during rollback to schema 0

migrations.up: create the immutable action verification boundary; widen schema_version bound to 7
migrations.down: drop the verification boundary during rollback to schema 0

migrations.up: create control authority head, append-only checkpoint journal, and append-only cutover authorizations; widen schema_version bound to 8
migrations.down: drop cutover authorizations, authority checkpoints, and the authority head during rollback to schema 0

migrations.up: widen the control operation journal result status to PROPOSED or APPLIED, preserving every row and the frozen immutability triggers; widen schema_version bound to 9
migrations.down: no down migration: a journal row that records an applied result cannot be rewritten as a proposal

promotion_preconditions: the deployment opened the store with the cutover-authority capability (default off)
a control-authority-v1 checkpoint is installed as the live authority head
the presented checkpoint is that live tip (generation and digest)
the transition is legal, and the revision, epoch and fencing token expectations match
cutover.de_promotion: requires no authority so ownership is always recoverable

production_authority.source: the durable control_cutover record, read through store.IsGoAuthoritative(domain)
production_authority.self_assertion: rejected: WithAuthoritative(true) is a claim that must be backed by the durable record, and a larger epoch is never authority
production_authority.non_authoritative_path: unchanged qualification path; it does not consult the cutover record
production_authority.refusal: CUTOVER_NOT_AUTHORIZED before any durable write, with the cutover record left untouched

authority_claim.body: a control-authority-v1 checkpoint, bounded to 16 MiB and checked by the store for integrity, live chain, writer lease and deployment capability
authority_claim.success: 200 with head and advanced; an exact replay returns advanced=false without a second journal append
authority_claim.unclaimed_head: GET /internal/authority/head returns 404 CONTROL_AUTHORITY_NOT_CLAIMED before the first claim
authority_claim.refusals: 400 malformed or null checkpoint, 413 oversized checkpoint, 409 invalid chain or disabled cutover capability

mutation_apply.body: the exact canonical control-mutation-request-v2 document bytes
mutation_apply.authority: the signer public key, fleet id and environment come from DEEPSEEKD_MUTATION_SIGNER_KEY / DEEPSEEKD_FLEET_ID / DEEPSEEKD_ENVIRONMENT, never from the request
mutation_apply.refusal: 409 with the store error code (for example CUTOVER_NOT_AUTHORIZED)
mutation_apply.success: 200 with the operation result; a retry of the same operation is ALREADY_APPLIED and never applies twice

internal_api.peer: loopback-only, independent of the listener address
internal_api.anonymous_deployment: routes stay mounted but every request answers 401 INTERNAL_API_UNAUTHORIZED
internal_api.cutover_coupling: DEEPSEEKD_CONTROL_AUTHORITY is refused unless an internal API bearer is configured, so the migration authority cannot be claimed over an unauthenticated channel

checkpoints.chain: monotonic generation; previous digest must match the live tip

binds: previous and next revision, epoch and fencing token

authority.claim: store.ClaimControlAuthority advances the head; it is the only path that installs production control authority, reachable through bearer-guarded POST /internal/authority/claim
authority.deployment_gate: store.OpenOptions.AuthorizeCutover, taken from DEEPSEEKD_CONTROL_AUTHORITY, which config refuses unless an internal API bearer is configured
open_gaps: no per-domain externally signed promotion request exists yet
no provider-backed kill/takeover reconciliation evidence exists yet
no production ownership cutover or exact-head release evidence exists yet

operations.result_status: PROPOSED for a v1 proposal; APPLIED for a v2 apply-mutation
operations.production_apply_scope: reachable over the authenticated internal plane at POST /internal/mutation/apply (the body is the canonical v2 document; the signer key is deployment configuration, never caller-supplied). Verification parity is complete across Python, Go and Rust (compat v32, 34 cases).
operations.production_apply_reason: the frozen control-mutation-request-v1 carries exactly one intent, shadow-compare, whose payload is a comparison expectation with no record body; it cannot authorize a production mutation, and reinterpreting it as one is forbidden. Acceptance is therefore refused once the domain is Go-authoritative, before any durable write.
operations.production_apply_contract_revision: control-mutation-request-v2 (compat v32): operation apply-mutation, payload field recordPayload, and a distinct signature domain. Applied by Control.ApplyMutation, which requires the deployment cutover capability, a durably Go-authoritative domain, the live cutover revision/epoch/fencing token, the request's actionId + executionEpoch, and the record body the signer committed to.
operations.production_apply_atomicity: the record write, the operation journal row and the control event are one transaction; a retry of the same operation is idempotent and never applies twice
operations.shadow_write_guard: shadow persistence uses PutShadow, which checks the durable cutover in the write transaction for every domain; direct Put also refuses unsigned writes to promoted non-fenced control domains. A promoted domain cannot be mutated through the shadow API instead of the signed v2 apply channel
production_apply_refusals: no cutover capability or a domain that is not durably Go-authoritative
a fenced domain (action/scheduler_run/wave/transfer) whose mutations belong to the lease and admission path
a stale cutover revision, epoch or fencing token
a record revision that is not the next one
a record body carrying secret material, or one using floats
reuse of an operation ID in a different control domain, even with an identical payload digest

companion_stores.schema: CREATE TABLE tasks (id TEXT PRIMARY KEY, revision INTEGER NOT NULL, state TEXT NOT NULL, document BLOB NOT NULL)
